questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Explain how actors represent a situation through roles and action.
questions.prompt: One pupil reads a notice about a missing library key. Two others take the roles of a librarian and a pupil searching for the key and act out their encounter. Explain what makes the second presentation a drama.
questions.answer: The pupils take on characters and enact a situation through their actions and dialogue. The audience sees the encounter develop as the characters respond to each other.
questions.explanation: Drama presents imagined or represented situations through enacted roles.

markingGuide.description: Describes how actions or dialogue show the encounter unfolding.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Identify farce from features of a dramatic scene.
questions.prompt: In a school play, three characters repeatedly enter through the wrong doors and mistake one another for visitors. Their hurried movements and increasingly unlikely misunderstandings are intended to make the audience laugh. Which form of drama is most specifically suggested?
questions.explanation: Farce often creates comedy through exaggerated situations, rapid action and unlikely misunderstandings.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Describe two dance forms using information about how they are practised.
questions.prompt: A school programme describes one performance as a folk dance taught across generations in a community. It describes another as a contemporary dance piece in which pupils devised movements for a story about travelling to school. Use one detail from each description to explain the two dance-form labels.
questions.answer: The first is a folk dance in this programme because the movements are passed down as a community practice. The second is presented as contemporary dance because pupils devised new expressive movement for the story.
questions.explanation: Transmission is relevant to the first description, and the documented creative approach supports the label for the second. New choreography alone does not determine the form of every dance.

markingGuide.description: Connects the folk-dance label to community transmission.
Connects the contemporary label to the pupils’ devised expressive movement in this programme.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Explain how skill and design choices contribute to making a craft object.
questions.prompt: A pupil binds folded card and scrap paper into a small notebook. Its cover protects the pages, and the pupil adds a woven-paper border. Explain how the object shows two aspects of craft.
questions.answer: Binding the pages securely shows skill in making a useful object. Adding the border shows a decorative choice that changes how the notebook looks.
questions.explanation: A craft object can combine skilled construction with useful and decorative features.

markingGuide.description: Identifies a skilled or functional feature.
Connects the two features to the making of a craft object.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Construct and test a freestanding craft object from available material.
questions.prompt: Using teacher-provided card, a ruler and tape, make a tabletop holder for one name card. The holder should stand on its own and keep the name visible. Show your teacher a feature that prevents it from tipping.
questions.answer: One solution is to fold card into a broad triangular stand and tape the join. A folded lip holds the name card in front. The broad base supports the holder when the card is in place.
questions.explanation: The making task connects material choice, joining and testing to a useful purpose.

markingGuide.description: Constructs a freestanding holder from card.
Uses a secure fold or join.
Demonstrates that a name card stays visible in the holder.
Identifies a feature that helps the holder stay upright.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.subtopic: Materials and tools in a paper mosaic
questions.learningObjective: Choose materials and tools for a flat classroom mosaic.
questions.prompt: A group is making a paper mosaic on card. It needs small flat pieces, a way to secure them and a tool to trim pieces at the edges. Which set provides all three?
questions.answer: Coloured paper shapes, a glue stick and classroom scissors.
questions.explanation: The paper pieces act as tesserae, the glue fixes them to the support and the scissors trim pieces to fit.
options: A ruler, a pencil and an eraser.
Coloured paper shapes, a ruler and a pencil.
A glue stick, a ruler and an eraser.
Coloured paper shapes, a glue stick and classroom scissors.
